metadata.audience: English-speaking independent visitors interested in ceramics, art, design and material culture, 2–5 days
metadata.promise: Jingdezhen is a living ceramic system: materials, kilns, labour, imperial standards, markets, artists and contemporary experimentation—not a porcelain shopping stop.
metadata.commercial_boundary: Research and human-checked digital roadbook only. No artist access, class/residency/admission promise, ceramic authentication, purchase/shipping/export service, booking or bundled-travel sales.

source_policy.rule: Heritage access, studio availability, markets, exhibitions, courses, firing, safety, shipping and artist visits are dynamic; all require current human validation.

sources.title: UNESCO Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites
UNESCO Imperial Kiln Sites tentative list

modules.name: Porcelain as a system
modules.question: What do material, labour, kiln, design and trade reveal together?
modules.output_rule: Begin with a process question, not a shopping list.

modules.name: Imperial kiln and technical history
modules.question: How did standards, management and technique shape porcelain?
modules.output_rule: Use heritage/public interpretation with current access check.

modules.name: Contemporary art and design ecology
modules.question: Do I want public art/design observation or a private artist encounter?
modules.output_rule: Only public/currently verified venues; private studios require release gate.

modules.name: Market, material and buying boundary
modules.question: Am I observing, collecting, buying a souvenir or sourcing?
modules.output_rule: No authentication, value, provenance, shipping or export claim.

modules.name: Courses, workshops, residency and apprenticeship
modules.question: Which level of making is actually intended?
modules.output_rule: Separate a short experience from professional learning or residency; all supplier claims gated.

modules.name: Kiln, dust, firing and work safety
modules.question: What risks or practical limits matter before a making encounter?
modules.output_rule: No workshop without safety, materials, firing, insurance and age/mobility checks.

modules.name: Pacing and ceramic-city comparison
modules.question: How many days does Jingdezhen need, and how does it differ from Dehua?
modules.output_rule: Two days for public system; three-plus days for a verified making/artist decision.

modules.name: Arrival, language and delivery friction
modules.question: Can the client navigate, pay, communicate and receive work safely?
modules.output_rule: Human-check all foreign-visitor and shipping assumptions.

points.name: Porcelain-system framing card
points.why_it_matters: The city makes sense when raw material, forming, glazing, firing, labour and trade are read as one system.
points.agent_use: Ask what part of the system interests the visitor.

points.name: Material/process observation decision
points.why_it_matters: A public process/heritage lens can make porcelain legible without requiring a private studio visit.
points.agent_use: Use only after public route verification.

points.name: Imperial kiln heritage decision
points.why_it_matters: A route into standards, management and technical history behind imperial porcelain production.
points.agent_use: Verify current access; avoid a generic dynasty lecture.

points.name: Technical innovation card
points.why_it_matters: Jingdezhen's contribution includes material and production innovation, such as the kaolin/porcelain-stone binary formula described by UNESCO.
points.agent_use: Translate technical context to client skill level.

points.name: Taoxichuan/public art decision
points.why_it_matters: A possible entry into contemporary ceramics, design, retail and artist ecology, without implying every object or studio is equivalent.
points.agent_use: Verify current public programme and distinguish observation from buying.

points.name: Public artist/design ecosystem lead
points.why_it_matters: A research lane for galleries, public events and artist networks, not private access brokerage.
points.agent_use: No artist introduction or visit promise.

points.name: Artist-studio access refusal
points.why_it_matters: Artists' studios are working/private spaces; a travel product must not turn them into on-demand attractions.
points.agent_use: Capture interest; require individual partner release.

points.name: Market observation decision
points.why_it_matters: Markets can show style, price range and contemporary production, but cannot verify provenance, quality or value.
points.agent_use: Separate observation from purchase; no product endorsement.

points.name: Ceramic purchase/shipping boundary
points.why_it_matters: The database cannot authenticate pieces or guarantee firing, packaging, customs, shipping, insurance or food safety.
points.agent_use: Give due-diligence questions only.

points.name: Short workshop intent card
points.why_it_matters: A one-off making experience is not a professional class, apprenticeship or residency.
points.agent_use: Ask desired outcome and departure date; do not promise a finished piece.

points.name: Residency/apprenticeship boundary
points.why_it_matters: Long-term study entails selection, visa, studio, finance and professional relationships outside a tourism roadbook.
points.agent_use: State boundary and collect research interest only.

points.name: Verified workshop release gate
points.why_it_matters: Any workshop needs safety, dust/kiln protocol, English/translation, group limit, firing/delivery and consent evidence.
points.agent_use: No quote/book until partner_ready evidence exists.

points.name: Firing/delivery reality card
points.why_it_matters: A visitor's work may not be fired before departure; this is a delivery and breakage decision, not a souvenir guarantee.
points.agent_use: Ask departure and shipping tolerance early.

points.name: Two-day Jingdezhen core
points.why_it_matters: Two days can cover a heritage/process lens plus a public contemporary/market layer, not a verified making encounter by default.
points.agent_use: No private studio or workshop promise.

points.name: Four-day making/artist decision
points.why_it_matters: Only with more days can a visitor reasonably add a verified workshop or deeper public art/design investigation.
points.agent_use: Still requires partner release.

points.name: Jingdezhen–Dehua comparison
points.why_it_matters: Jingdezhen is a broad technical/imperial/contemporary ceramic ecology; Dehua is a more focused Fujian production/design extension. They should not be collapsed.
points.agent_use: Ask material-history, contemporary art or production-network preference.

points.name: Shanghai/Hangzhou handoff
points.why_it_matters: The city can follow Shanghai/Hangzhou art/design interests, but needs protected travel time rather than a casual day trip.
points.agent_use: No live travel claims or package.

points.name: Arrival/payment/language audit
points.why_it_matters: Payment, data, translation, station arrival and workshop communication decide whether an independent visitor can participate confidently.
points.agent_use: Ask readiness before output.

points.name: Art-event seasonality card
points.why_it_matters: Markets, fairs, exhibitions and artist availability vary; static event listings should never be output as facts.
points.agent_use: Use date-specific check.

points.name: Ethical ceramic observation
points.why_it_matters: Workers, makers and studios deserve consent; a visitor should not obstruct, copy or photograph processes without permission.
points.agent_use: State consent and intellectual-property conduct.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you interested in material/process, imperial history, contemporary art, buying, a short workshop, or professional learning?
Do you want a one-off experience or genuine skills learning, and when do you depart relative to any firing/delivery?
Are you exploring a professional programme rather than tourism? Duration, visa, language and portfolio need a separate scope.
Are you browsing, buying for personal use, collecting, or arranging delivery? The roadbook cannot authenticate or ship objects.
Do you have two public-exploration days, or four-plus days for a separately verified making decision?
Do you want imperial/technical history and contemporary artist ecology, or a Fujian production/design extension?
Would you like a human-checked brief with official links while you make any bookings directly?

output_guardrails: Never promise artist, studio, kiln, course, residency, firing or private access.
Never authenticate, price, value, ship, export or guarantee ceramic objects.
Never confuse a short workshop with training, apprenticeship or residency.
Never place a workshop into two-day public core without partner release.
No booking, payment collection, packaging, guiding or third-party experience sales.

launch_checks.name: Heritage/process field walk
launch_checks.purpose: Current public access and system narrative

launch_checks.name: Taoxichuan/market audit
launch_checks.purpose: Public programme, commercial noise and purchase boundary

launch_checks.name: Workshop safety/firing audit
launch_checks.purpose: Dust, kiln, language, delivery and commercial evidence
